about.title: Solana Beach Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A small coastal city like Solana Beach still sees its share of injuries tied to consumer goods, vehicle components, household equipment, and recreational gear used along the beach and bluffs. Under California law, these claims frequently rest on strict liability, meaning an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product itself was defective in design, manufacturing, or warning, and that the defect caused harm. That standard can apply to the company that made the item, the distributor who moved it through the supply chain, or the retailer who sold it locally. Because San Diego County residents shop both online and in person, tracking down every responsible party can get complicated fast. Our team handles product liability claims directly and can review what happened and explain your options. If a product is involved, hold onto it exactly as it is; it may be the most important piece of evidence you have.
commonInjuries: Burns from malfunctioning appliances or batteries
Lacerations from faulty tools or machinery
Traumatic injuries from failed vehicle parts or airbags
Poisoning or illness from contaminated goods
Fractures from collapsing furniture or equipment
Injuries from defective recreational or sporting gear

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Your Claim

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Because California applies strict liability to defective products, the focus stays on the product's condition and the harm it caused, not on digging up carelessness by the manufacturer.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can each be pulled into a claim, which matters in a place like Solana Beach where products often pass through several hands before reaching a buyer.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Your Evidence
items.desc: Since defect claims hinge on the item's design, manufacturing, or missing warnings, preserving the exact product in its post-incident condition can be critical to building your case.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless to have a case?
items.answer: No. California's strict liability rule generally means you only need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. Negligence isn't the required standard, which can simplify what you need to establish.

items.question: I was hurt by gear I used near the Solana Beach bluffs or beach access points. Does that matter?
items.answer: It can help establish where and how the product failed, but the underlying legal analysis is the same regardless of location within San Diego County. What matters most is preserving the product and documenting the circumstances of the injury.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it in the same condition it was in right after the incident — don't repair, discard, or alter it. Our team can advise on how it should be stored or inspected as part of reviewing your claim.

items.question: Does your firm represent me in my product liability claim?
items.answer: Yes. Our team handles product liability claims and will work with you on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless you recover.
